summary: Structural + security mastermind audit of YURI-OS + Yuri-as-agent: produce a code-verified de-bloat cut list, security hardening findings, hook/gate consolidation, memory consolidation, and a compounding-simplification roadmap that makes the owner's use simpler but more powerful.

subtasks.prompt: Audit Yuri-as-agent attack surface: untrusted-input (read_doc/screen/mail/fleet-output) -> critical-action paths, regex confirm-gate bypass, 3 drifted protected-path denylists (bash-security-guard / yuri-safety-core / yuri-z-brain regex), exfiltration, auto-hook supply chain, overnight/unattended risk. Rank findings + minimal mitigations.

Consolidation shortlist: collapse the overlapping gate layers, dispatch surfaces (5-6 routers, retire the dead ones), and memory writers to a canonical set; code-verify each cut candidate (not registry-guess).

The 13 PreToolUse hooks fire on every tool call. Identify which are advisory theater vs real enforcement, the per-call tax, and the merge/cut candidates that reduce it without losing the 3 real gates.
320 memory files, 23-35 semantic dups across ~4 rule families, MEMORY.md over cap. Consolidation plan: merge dup feedback families to canonical rules, archive settled projects, cap the Active index.

Adversarially verify every proposed cut against code before it lands — a sibling lane already found the inventory over-claimed dead/redundant items that were actually live. Separate CONFIRMED-dead from NEEDS-VERIFICATION.
SOUL/persona/yuri-origin ~404 lines/session with 15 overlapping concepts, zero contradictions. Surgical dedup vs single-spine — keep separation-of-concerns, replace dup lines with cross-references.
Sequence the cuts + hardening into a compounding roadmap: each step makes the next easier; the owner's use gets simpler but more powerful. Name the single highest-leverage first move.
